name: Grant writing and grant research for nonprofits and startups (flat fee)
summary: Research matching grants and draft applications (narratives, budgets justifications, LOIs) for nonprofits, researchers and startups at a flat or hourly fee.
howItWorks: Nonprofits, labs and startups pay because applications are long and deadline-driven. You track public RFPs, use an LLM to draft narratives from the client's own facts, and edit to each funder's rubric. Charge per application or retainer, not a % of the award (commission pricing is considered unethical and often barred from grant funds). Clients reapply every cycle.

payout.notes: Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer service fee set per contract since May 2025 (pre-May-2025 contracts 10%), per Upwork's SEC 10-Q; Upwork help pages block automated fetch. Fiverr: 20% seller fee and 14-day clearance (7 days for Top Rated) are widely reported but Fiverr's help center blocked fetch, so not confirmed from the official page. Re-checked Nov 2026: fiverr.com and help.fiverr.com still return 403, the Wayback Machine is unreachable, and Fiverr's FY2025 Form 20-F gives only a blended 27.7% take rate. Unconfirmed: Fiverr's 20% seller fee, 14-day (7-day Top Rated) clearance, and the $1 PayPal / $20 Payoneer bank withdrawal minimums.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Never fabricate data, outcomes or letters of support; the applicant signs and is responsible for submissions.
complianceRequirements: flat/hourly fees, no award contingency (GPA/AFP ethics-code norm; both sites blocked fetch, unconfirmed)

availability.notes: Upwork/Fiverr pay out in nearly all reference countries via Payoneer/bank.

manualSteps: discovery call to gather true facts
client sign-off and submission by client
risks: awards outside your control drive client churn
evidence: Grant writing is a standing Upwork/Fiverr category; rates and success rates not verified.

Fiverr seller account + ID verification

name: Compliant B2B cold-email lead generation service
summary: Run opt-out-compliant B2B outbound email campaigns that book sales meetings for clients, paid per month or per qualified meeting.
howItWorks: B2B firms pay for booked meetings. You define the ideal customer, source business contacts from licensed data vendors, personalize emails with an LLM, and send low-volume campaigns from client domains with unsubscribe link and postal address. Replies are triaged and meetings booked. Honor opt-outs (US: 10 business days) and consent rules of each recipient country.

payout.notes: Net-7 to net-30 invoices; take 30-50% deposits. Stripe is not offered in many reference countries (stripe.com/global, Nov 2026: absent in e.g. the Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Sri Lanka, Tunisia, Ecuador, Serbia; Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa only via its extended network); Payoneer covers 190+ countries and territories.

restrictedIn: Germany (recipients: UWG s.7(2) no.2 requires prior express consent for email ads to any addressee, incl. businesses)
Netherlands (recipients: Telecommunicatiewet art. 11.7(1) consent also applies to legal persons)
Canada (recipients: CASL consent; implied only for conspicuously published addresses relevant to the recipient's role)
legality.notes: Restrictions are on recipients located in these countries, not on where the operator lives. US: CAN-SPAM has no B2B exception but is opt-out (honor within 10 business days). UK: ICO confirms PECR email consent rule does not cover corporate subscribers (companies, LLPs, Scottish partnerships); sole traders and some partnerships need consent or soft opt-in. Germany and Canada verified from statute; Netherlands from secondary sources (statute page not parsed). Other likely opt-in recipient markets (Italy, South Korea, Japan partially) not verified, so coverage kept at 88 (~44/50) rather than 94. Never email consumers or use scraped lists.
complianceRequirements: CAN-SPAM: honest headers, postal address, opt-out in 10 business days

availability.notes: Direct invoicing works almost everywhere; legality depends on recipient country, not operator country.

automationPlan: ICP filtering and enrichment from licensed data
fullCycle: Pick a niche with US/UK B2B targets
risks: fines (US up to $53,088 per violating email)
evidence: FTC CAN-SPAM guide: no B2B exception, opt-out within 10 business days, penalties up to $53,088 per email, so compliant outbound agencies operate legally in the US; ICO confirms UK corporate subscribers can be emailed without prior consent.

name: Split-fee recruiting on Paraform and BountyJobs
summary: Independent recruiters fill open roles posted on recruiting marketplaces and earn a share of the employer's placement fee.
howItWorks: Employers post roles with a fixed fee or % of salary. You source candidates with AI-assisted search and outreach, submit those who consent, and are paid after hire and guarantee. Paraform pays the listed per-role reward (its recruiter page shows an 80% success-fee split example); BountyJobs vets agencies by niche. Closing candidates stays human work.

methods: Paraform -> Stripe payout to recruiter's chosen method (bank)
payout.frequency: per placement: Paraform in thirds at 30/60/90 days after start; BountyJobs after employer pays + 60 days
payout.notes: Paraform Recruiting Agreement: reward is fixed or % of first-year salary; paid 1/3 at 30, 60 and 90 days after the candidate's start date via Stripe; 90-day guarantee with repayment/clawback if no replacement search. BountyJobs FAQ: earnings pending until the employer pays and 60 days of employment elapse; 60-day guarantee (fixed fees or <20% of salary) or 90-day (>=20%). Unconfirmed (BountyJobs FAQ re-checked Nov 2026): the payout method BountyJobs uses to pay agencies and any platform fee it deducts are not published.

legality.notes: Legal; some countries license fee-charging placement (Japan: MHLW permission under the Employment Security Act; South Korea: registration under its Employment Security Act; Philippines: DOLE/DMW licensing). These generally bite when placing candidates in or from those countries; listed from legal knowledge, government pages not re-fetched (search budget exhausted). Candidate data is personal data; consent required before submission.

availability.notes: Roles mostly US. Paraform has active UK recruiters and its agreement covers international Stripe transfers, but no country list is published; BountyJobs states no country rule and vets agencies (niche or preferred-vendor) within 72h. ~50% payout availability is an estimate. Recruiter.com dropped: it now sells flat-fee on-demand recruiting, not a split-fee marketplace.

fee clawback if hire leaves early
vetting excludes newcomers; mostly US roles

name: WCAG accessibility audits and remediation
summary: Audit websites/apps/PDFs against WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA, deliver prioritized reports and fix code or documents.
howItWorks: Companies and public bodies pay as accessibility laws tighten (US ADA Title II rule; EU Accessibility Act covers e-commerce). Scanners find part of the issues; you add keyboard/screen-reader testing, write the report with LLM help, and fix code or tag PDFs. Monitoring retainers follow.

payout.notes: Net-7 to net-30 invoices; take 30-50% deposits. Stripe missing in many reference countries; Wise/Payoneer cover most.

legality.notes: Legal; taxable. Audits are opinions, not legal advice; avoid 'guaranteed compliant' or certification claims.
complianceRequirements: authorized testing on client properties only

availability.notes: Direct invoicing works almost everywhere; demand concentrated in US/EU/UK/Canada/Australia clients.

automationPlan: LLM-written issue descriptions and fix snippets
risks: automated tools find only part of issues, so skill matters
evidence: WebAIM Million 2026 (Feb 2026): 95.9% of top home pages had detected WCAG 2 failures, avg 56.1 errors. DOJ Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA): compliance dates extended by an April 20, 2026 interim final rule to April 26, 2027 (pop. 50k+) and April 26, 2028 (smaller). EU Accessibility Act covers e-commerce.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order.

Credentials (e.g. IAAP CPACC/WAS) help win buyers; without them first sales are slow.
